Generator recipes (generator.*)

Reference Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-20 Source: recipe.rs

A recipe is the editable graph behind anything a generator baked. It is a file next to the product, so the source of a texture, material, tree, lake or terrain is never lost.

1. File type#

<name>.generator.<kind>, one kind per generator:

File Generator Product beside it
Bark.generator.texture Texture Generator Bark.png
Rock.generator.material Material Generator Rock.mat
Oak.generator.nature Nature Generator oak_trunk.obj, oak_leaves.obj
Lake.generator.water Water Generator lake.mat
Alpine.generator.terrain Terrain Generator alpine_height.png

The file is JSON: format (caffeine-generator), version, kind, name, product, graph (the generator's own text form) and generator_version, the algorithm version the recipe was authored with (files without it read as 1; new files write 2, the same number as Caffeine::Core::GENERATOR_VERSION). Each generator still owns its graph format; the recipe only wraps it. A file written by a newer Doppio is refused with a message instead of being misread. The engine lists these files with asset kind generator.

2. Behaviour#

  • Saving, exporting or placing a generator's result writes its recipe beside the product: Place in scene in the Nature, Water and Terrain tabs saves the graph too, so nothing placed is ever a dead end. Water and Terrain write the recipe before they touch the scene, so a failure while placing never loses the graph; the recipe is in Water/ or Terrain/ beside the material or height map and shows in the Assets pane as soon as it is written.
  • Double-click a recipe, or a baked asset that has one, to reopen the graph in its generator.
  • Imported assets have no recipe, so double-click behaves as before (a picture becomes a new material). A MaterialCraft archive is the exception because it carries its graph.
  • Older sidecars (.mgraph, .texgraph, .nature, .water, .terrain-graph) are still found and opened; the next save writes the new file.
  • Multi-part products (oak_trunk.obj) find the Nature or Terrain recipe whose name prefixes theirs.
  • A recipe may list the files it wrote in products (paths relative to the assets root). The Nature recipe does.
  • Agents and tests reopen a graph with the open_generator action (Message::OpenGeneratorFor): the path may be a recipe, a .prefab, or anything a generator baked.

A tree is a bundle#

Placing or exporting a Nature model writes everything it is made of, so it can be edited, reused and shared:

File What it is
Models/Nature/oak_trunk.obj, oak_leaves.obj the meshes
Materials/Nature/*.mat and Textures/Nature/*.png one material per part, with its maps
Models/Nature/oak.generator.nature the graph, plus products: every file above
Materials/Nature/<name>.generator.material the Material Generator graph of each library material (ground, needles…); never overwritten once you have edited it
Prefabs/oak.prefab the tree as placed (group, parts, material slots, Micromesh switches), pointing back at its recipe

Bark, rock and leaf-card surfaces are generated by the Nature graph itself, so the nature recipe is their recipe. Export builds the same bundle without leaving the tree in the scene.

2b. Prefabs (*.prefab)#

A prefab is a JSON snapshot of an entity tree by what the Inspector shows: every component and field, by name (uikit/prefab_file.rs, format caffeine-prefab). The first entity is the root, saved at the origin; generator names the recipe it came from. Double-click a prefab in the Assets pane (or call the place_prefab action) to drop a copy at the camera focus; it is one undo step. Water and terrain are engine-side surfaces rather than component fields, so they get a recipe but no prefab.

3. Folders#

Folders the editor creates are capitalised: Assets/Raw/{Animations,Audio,Generators,Materials,Models,Prefabs,Sky,TextureSets,Textures}, Assets/Processed, Scripts, Scenes, Build, and Nature, Terrain, Water for generator output. Existing projects keep their own names; renaming is the user's choice.

4. caf-pack#

.generator.* files are sources, not assets to pack. caf-pack now has an explicit rule (Registry::isEditorOnly): recipes and the older graph sidecars (.mgraph, .texgraph, .nature, .water, .terrain-graph) are skipped and listed (Skipped editor-only source: ...) instead of failing the package with "No processor registered". Packer::getSkipped() returns the list. Covered by tests/test_cafpack_editor_only.cpp (the change lives in the caf-pack submodule).

5. Referencing recipes#

Generators point at recipes, not at finished models: a vegetation generator reruns an Oak recipe for variants and adapts the result to the terrain. The resolver is uikit/recipe_ref.rs.

  • [x] Slots. The Nature Your Material (.mat) and Your Texture (PNG) nodes and the Terrain layer slots accept a generator.material / generator.texture path. A texture recipe is baked beside itself when its PNG is missing; a material recipe must have been baked once (the error says so). A recipe of the wrong kind is refused with a message.
  • [x] Variants, cached. bake_nature_variant(recipe, seed, quality, cache_dir) reseeds every node's seed from the variant seed and writes the OBJ parts into <cache>/<name>_<key>/; the key hashes the recipe's graph, its generator_version, the seed and the quality, so editing the recipe invalidates the cache. Seed 0 keeps the authored seeds. nature_variants derives N seeds from a base seed. CLI: doppio-material variants Oak.generator.nature --out DIR --count 8 --seed 3.
  • [x] Same numbers in both languages. derive_seed/unit are SplitMix64, bit for bit Caffeine::Core::deriveSeed/toUnit; the golden tests in tests/test_hash.cpp and recipe_ref.rs pin the same values.
  • [x] generator_version in every recipe.
  • [ ] Water: its material comes from the Water Material node, which already writes Water/<name>.mat; a recipe slot is not wired.
  • [ ] On-demand bake of a material recipe (needs the engine session the Material Generator uses).
  • [ ] A scatter or vegetation generator that consumes nature_variants and places the results on a terrain.
